evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'we can be able to get you an accurate code so you, that you can depend on we'll just need to ask you some a few questions in order for us to do so, this would take within the next five to ten minutes of your time. Would that be okay?' — framing is present (time-boxed + dependable quote promise) but not perfectly recognizable, and moves forward without strongly waiting for confirmation.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Peng Tang), moving day (November 7th), city-to-city route (whiskey way apartment to storage facility in Allen, Texas), and approximate size (two-bedroom apartment) — all four covered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks 'Do you have any biggest concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer?' but only after already asking when they're moving and checking availability. Customer responds 'No, I've used you all this will be the fourth time' — agenda asked, but after probing started.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (two-bedroom apartment), floor (eleventh floor), rooms (confirmed two bedroom only, no other spaces), walking distance (30 feet from parking to elevator, 15 feet from elevator to unit), additional rooms (none), special considerations (reserved elevator, TV only, no large items), and second stop (indoor storage facility, first floor, 10x15, loading dock). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep explicitly asks 'do we have flexibility with regards to the of the date because our best value days is every Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays' — wait, incorrect cite. Actually: 'do we have help in packing. Is that correct?' — packing offered and customer declines.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep states: 'the typical backs count for your home size is 25 to 35 box is, do you feel that you fall within that range?' Customer responds 'Probably less than that.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides: 'Normally it would take two movers between three and a half to five and a half hours to completely move' and personalizes: 'In your case we're coming from a two bedroom apartment located on the eleventh floor with a reserve elevator going to the new location, we just like thirty minutes away from the first location, this is a storage unit. So, we'll send out two movers and one truck estimated time is between four and a half to five and a half hours, the estimated cost in case they end up five and a half hours would be $1,296' — anchored to typical range and personalized to specific move.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses trip fee upfront: 'The only thing that is outside ore weight would be the trip fee. There is a trip fee of 75 dollars other than that everything is already included.' Also frames 2.5-hour minimum: 'for any move we have a minimum of two and a half hours once you go over that it will always be prorated into fifteen minute increments.' Both elements present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly to booking: 'So just wanted to let you know that on the 7th of November we can be able to book your slot as early as 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM there's no deposit required' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep mentions 'We still have the same perks that we have before. We still have no worry damage coverage on time guarantee' but does not specify the discount terms (starts discounting immediately if late). Mentioned but vague.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep says 'We still have the same perks that we have before. We still have no worry damage coverage on time guarantee' but provides no details about $2,000 coverage, no deductible, no fine print, or that it's built into the rate. Mentioned but missing critical framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' after presenting the Two Promises. Customer had raised price concerns repeatedly ('your prices have gone up dramatically'), but rep does not address whether those concerns are resolved.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'do you still have concerns or any questions before I let you go?' — a throwaway version of the genuine check. Not the 'What's still concerning you about this move?' formulation.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks 'truly believe that we're the best mover in town. Do you want me to lock that in for you?' — direct and explicit, no easy-out softening.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep states 'there's no deposit required' and 'No reason securing your spot in case if you wanted to reschedule or to cancel then all you have to do is just simply give us a call at anytime' — rate-lock concept covered (no deposit, hold the slot).
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirms date (November 7th), time (8:30 AM to 9:00 AM), and notes upcoming confirmation email with date/time/phone. Missing explicit phone number confirmation, arrival window detail beyond the single time window given, addresses confirmation, and crew-specific notes about customer concerns (price sensitivity, prior move history).

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, floor, distances, special items, secondary location specifics) and provided a fully anchored, personalized estimate range tied directly to the customer's two-bedroom, elevated layout and 30-minute distance to storage.
coaching_note: After pricing discussion, skip the automatic pivot to booking and ask 'Does that feel fair?' with genuine silence — then address the customer's stated price sensitivity before closing; the Two Promises also need to specify discount terms (On-Time) and deductible/coverage details (Damage) rather than generic mentions of prior perks.
booking_note: Customer explicitly agreed to lock in the move when asked 'Do you want me to lock that in for you?' and responded 'Yes please.' Date (November 7th) and time window (8:30-9:00 AM) were confirmed.
